instructions:
This server exposes the R package tidybrreg 0.6.0 as tools. Tool names are the package's exported function names; every description is the function's help page.

A tidy interface to query and download data from the Norwegian Central Coordinating Register for Legal Entities (Enhetsregisteret), maintained by the Br?nn?ysund Register Centre. Looks up entities, sub-entities, roles, corporate groups and signing authority, searches the register, reads the change data capture feeds, and downloads the bulk register. Returns tibbles with English column names mapped via a data-driven dictionary; unknown API fields pass through with auto-generated names, and only observed fields are emitted. Coded values (legal forms, industry codes, roles) can be translated to English or Norwegian using bundled reference data or live lookups from the Statistics Norway 'KLASS' API. Register data is published under the Norwegian Licence for Open Government Data (NLOD 2.0).

Working rules, as the package documents them:

- Coded values are returned as codes (legal forms, NACE, sector, roles). Translate with brreg_label or type = "label" only when the user wants descriptions.

- Entity results emit only the fields the register carried for that entity; a missing column means the register did not emit it, not that the value is empty.

- A warning or an attribute such as complete = FALSE, total_matches, http_status or deleted = TRUE is part of the answer: report it to the user rather than presenting a slice as the whole population.

- Organization numbers are 9-digit strings validated with modulus 11; quote them as strings.

- Bulk downloads are large (tens to hundreds of megabytes); prefer brreg_search for interactive questions.

- Register data is published by the Brønnøysund Register Centre under NLOD 2.0 and must be attributed when redistributed.

# tidybrreg_conditions: Conditions signalled by tidybrreg

Every error and warning raised by the package carries a class that can be caught with `tryCatch()` or silenced with `suppressWarnings()` selectively, and a set of fields describing the request that produced it. All classes inherit from `tidybrreg_error` or `tidybrreg_warning`.

## Errors

- `tidybrreg_error_invalid_org_nr`: the organization number failed `brreg_validate()`. Field `org_nr`.
- `tidybrreg_error_invalid_filter`: a filter is not supported by the requested registry (for example `bankrupt` on `underenheter`). Fields `registry`, `filter`.
- `tidybrreg_error_not_found`: the endpoint answered HTTP 404 for an organization number. Fields `org_nr`, `endpoint`, `status`.
- `tidybrreg_error_http`: any other HTTP status of 400 or above, or a failure on the first page of a paginated request. Fields `endpoint`, `status`, `messages` (as extracted from the BRREG error body).
- `tidybrreg_error_result_window`: the query matches more entities than BRREG's search window can deliver and the request asked for more than the window. Fields `endpoint`, `total_matches`, `retrieval_limit`, `filters`. See `brreg_search()`.

## Warnings

- `tidybrreg_warning_deleted`: the entity has been deleted from the register (HTTP 410, or HTTP 200 with `respons_klasse` `"SlettetEnhet"`). Fields `org_nr`, `deletion_date`.
- `tidybrreg_warning_partial`: a paginated request failed after at least one page was retrieved; the partial result is returned with attribute `complete = FALSE`. Fields `endpoint`, `status`, `pages_fetched`.
- `tidybrreg_warning_truncated`: more results exist than were returned because of `max_results` or `max_pages`; the result carries attribute `complete = FALSE`. Fields `endpoint`, `returned`, `total_matches`.
- `tidybrreg_warning_unknown_member`: an update feed carried a member the package does not model; it is passed through unchanged. Field `members`.
- `tidybrreg_warning_bundled_fallback`: SSB KLASS was unreachable and a bundled dictionary was used instead. Fields `dictname`, `vintage`.
- `tidybrreg_warning_parse`: values could not be coerced to the type declared in field_dict; the result carries attribute `brreg_parse_problems`. Field `n`.

## See also

Other tidybrreg utilities: `brreg_label()`, `brreg_validate()`, `get_brreg_dic()`, `tidybrreg_endpoints`

## Examples

```r
tryCatch( brreg_entity("123456789"), tidybrreg_error_invalid_org_nr = function(e) e$org_nr )
```

tools.name: brreg_children
tools.title: Get child entities in the organisational hierarchy
tools.description:
Query the enheter registry for entities whose `overordnetEnhet` matches the given org number. This traverses the ORGL parent-child hierarchy (e.g. Stortinget to Riksrevisjonen), which is distinct from the enhet-to-underenhet relationship and from the konsern ownership tree returned by `brreg_konsern()`.

tools.name: brreg_download
tools.title: Download the full Norwegian business register
tools.description:
Download a complete extract of the Central Coordinating Register for Legal Entities (~1 million entities, ~150 MB gzipped). The bulk endpoint does not support server-side filtering — it always returns all entities. Use `brreg_search()` for filtered queries up to 10,000 results, or download the full register here and filter locally.

**Backend routing.** The brreg API has two data access paths with fundamentally different characteristics, following the cansim (Statistics Canada) pattern of separate functions for separate access patterns rather than the eurostat pattern of auto-routing within one function:

- **`brreg_search()`**: JSON API with server-side filtering. Fast for small result sets, capped at 10,000. Interactive exploration.
- **`brreg_download()`**: Bulk CSV or JSON. Always returns the full register. Appropriate for any analysis requiring more than 10,000 entities.

Results from both paths use the same column names and types via field_dict; only observed columns are emitted (see `brreg_entity()`).

**Caching.** With `cache = TRUE` (default) the gzipped payload is stored in `tools::R_user_dir("tidybrreg", "cache")` together with a sidecar recording the server's `ETag` and `Last-Modified` validators, and a later call reuses it. `refresh = TRUE` forces a new download. `refresh = "auto"` sends a HEAD request and re-downloads when either validator differs from the sidecar; when the sidecar is missing or the server sends neither validator, nothing can prove the cache current, so it is re-downloaded. With `cache = FALSE` the payload goes to a temporary file that is deleted after parsing; with `type_output = "path"` that temporary path is returned and the caller owns it. The cache directory is created only by this function, never at load time.

Metadata of the most recent download (`url`, `etag`, `last_modified` as a UTC `POSIXct`, `downloaded_at`, `path`) is available as `attr(result, "brreg_download")` on tibble output.

**Returns.** Depends on `type_output`:

- `"tibble"`: A tibble with ~1 million rows. Column names mapped via field_dict. For `type = "roller"`, one row per role assignment with the columns of `brreg_roles()`.
- `"path"`: Character file path to the gzipped download.

**Output shaping (server-side).** `.limit` rows (default 200), `.offset`, `.columns`, `.format` (records, csv, markdown). The structured result reports `n_total`, the attributes tidybrreg attached (for example `total_matches`, `complete`, `http_status`) and every warning tidybrreg signalled, with its condition class.

type.description: One of `"enheter"` (main entities, default), `"underenheter"` (sub-entities / establishments), or `"roller"` (all roles for all entities). Roller data is only available as JSON via `/roller/totalbestand` (~131 MB).

format.description: Download format: `"csv"` (default for enheter/underenheter, comma-delimited) or `"json"` (JSON array). Only the JSON bulk carries `historiskeNavn`; the CSV has no such column. Roller bulk download is always JSON regardless of this parameter.

refresh.description: `FALSE` (default): use cached file if available. `TRUE`: force re-download. `"auto"`: revalidate against the server and re-download only when the cached copy cannot be shown current. Any other value is an error.

cache.description: Logical. If `TRUE` (default), keep the downloaded file in the persistent cache directory; if `FALSE`, use a temporary file.

type_output.description: One of `"tibble"` (default) or `"path"` (returns the file path without parsing).

.limit.description: Maximum number of rows to return from the result.

.offset.description: Number of rows to skip before returning.

.columns.description: Columns to keep (tidybrreg's English column names). Default: all.

.format.description: Text rendering of the rows in the content block.

tools.name: brreg_entity
tools.title: Look up a Norwegian legal entity
tools.description:
Retrieve registration details for a legal entity from Norway's Central Coordinating Register for Legal Entities (Enhetsregisteret), maintained by the Brønnøysund Register Centre. Every legal entity operating in Norway is assigned a unique 9-digit organization number and registered in this central register.

Column names are translated from Norwegian to English via the package field dictionary (field_dict). API fields not in the dictionary pass through with auto-generated snake_case names, so new fields added by brreg are never silently dropped. Use `brreg_label()` to translate coded values (legal forms, NACE codes) to English descriptions.

**Observed fields only.** The register emits only the fields that apply to an entity: a sole proprietorship (`ENK`) typically carries no `founding_date` or `employees`, a foreign branch (`NUF`) no `municipality_code`. The returned columns are exactly the fields the response carried, so every column other than `org_nr`, `registry` and `deleted` is conditionally present. Test for a column with `"x" %in% names(result)` rather than assuming it.

**Deleted entities.** BRREG reports a deleted entity either as HTTP 410 or, for most deletions, as HTTP 200 with `respons_klasse = "SlettetEnhet"` and a `slettedato`. Both are modelled the same way: `deleted` is `TRUE`, `deletion_date` is the parsed date, every other field the response carried is kept, and a `tidybrreg_warning_deleted` is signalled (silence it with `suppressWarnings(classes = "tidybrreg_warning_deleted")`). Live entities carry `deleted = FALSE`.

**Returns.** A tibble with one row and one column per field the API returned, named via field_dict, plus `registry` (which registry answered) and `deleted` (logical). Frequently present columns include `org_nr`, `name`, `legal_form`, `employees`, `founding_date`, `nace_1`, `municipality_code`, `bankrupt`, and `parent_org_nr`.

**Output shaping (server-side).** `.limit` rows (default 200), `.offset`, `.columns`, `.format` (records, csv, markdown). The structured result reports `n_total`, the attributes tidybrreg attached (for example `total_matches`, `complete`, `http_status`) and every warning tidybrreg signalled, with its condition class.

org_nr.description: Character. A single 9-digit Norwegian organization number. Validated using `brreg_validate()` before the API call; a vector of several numbers is an error (iterate with `lapply()`). Supply an ISO 8601 date (YYYY-MM-DD) or date-time (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ).

registry.description: One of `"auto"` (default, tries enheter then underenheter), `"enheter"` (main entities only), or `"underenheter"` (sub-entities only). Sub-entities have different fields (e.g. `overordnetEnhet` for the parent entity, `beliggenhetsadresse` instead of `forretningsadresse`).

type.description: A type of variables: `"code"` (default) returns raw codes, `"label"` returns English labels for coded columns (legal form, NACE, sector, etc.), following the eurostat package's pattern. Labelling NACE and sector codes consults SSB KLASS on first use in a session; see `get_brreg_dic()`.

.limit.description: Maximum number of rows to return from the result.

.offset.description: Number of rows to skip before returning.

.columns.description: Columns to keep (tidybrreg's English column names). Default: all.

.format.description: Text rendering of the rows in the content block.

rows.description: The returned slice of rows, one JSON object per row.

value.description: The result when it is not a table.

attributes.description: Metadata tidybrreg attached to the result (total_matches, complete, http_status, cursor, ...).

conditions.description: Warnings and messages tidybrreg signalled while producing the result.

tools.name: brreg_konsern
tools.title: Retrieve the corporate group structure (konsernstruktur)
tools.description:
Fetch the registered group hierarchy for a Norwegian legal entity from the Enhetsregisteret konsernstruktur endpoint (added by BRREG 2026-06-24). The tree is returned flat: one row per node, root included at `level = 0`, each child carrying its link form (`knytningsform`, e.g. `KDAT` "Konsern datter"), ownership basis (`grunnlag`, e.g. `"100%"`), and the registration date of the relation.

The JSON response omits `knytningsform` on the root node while the API's CSV variant emits it as `KKKK` "Øverste mor"; the root row is synthesized here to match the CSV semantics.

This is the ownership hierarchy and is distinct from `brreg_children()`, which searches `overordnetEnhet` — the administrative parent relation used in public-sector (ORGL) structures, not konsern ownership.

**404 semantics.** The endpoint returns 404 both for organization numbers that do not exist and for live entities that are not part of any registered group — the common case for ordinary companies. The `in_corporate_group` column from `brreg_entity()` disambiguates the two without a second lookup here.

**Status handling.** The per-entity endpoints behind `brreg_roles()`, `brreg_roles_legal()`, `brreg_konsern()`, `brreg_signatur()` and `brreg_prokura()` share one contract. HTTP 404 means the organization number is unknown to that endpoint, which for konsern, signatur and prokura is the ordinary case of an entity with nothing registered there: the typed zero-row tibble is returned with attribute `http_status = 404L` and no warning. HTTP 410 means the entity has been deleted: the typed zero-row tibble is returned with `http_status = 410L`, `deletion_date`, and a `tidybrreg_warning_deleted`. Any other status of 400 or above aborts with a `tidybrreg_error_http`. A successful response with nothing registered returns the typed zero-row tibble with no attribute. Use `brreg_entity()` to distinguish a non-existent organization number from a live entity with nothing registered.

**Returns.** A tibble with one row per node in the group tree. Columns: `org_nr` (the queried entity), `node_org_nr`, `node_name`, `level` (0 for the root), `link_form`, `link_form_desc`, `basis`, `relation_date` (Date), `parent_org_nr`, `parent_name`, `legal_form`, `legal_form_desc`. A zero-row tibble with the same typed columns if no group structure is registered.

**Output shaping (server-side).** `.limit` rows (default 200), `.offset`, `.columns`, `.format` (records, csv, markdown). The structured result reports `n_total`, the attributes tidybrreg attached (for example `total_matches`, `complete`, `http_status`) and every warning tidybrreg signalled, with its condition class.

tools.name: brreg_label
tools.title: Translate codes to human-readable labels
tools.description:
Replace coded values in a brreg tibble with English (or Norwegian) descriptions, following the eurostat package's `label_eurostat()` pattern. Works on both data frames and character vectors.

**Which columns are labelled.** `legal_form` (from legal_forms), `role_code` (from role_types), `role_group_code` (from role_groups), `nace_1`, `nace_2`, `nace_3` and `sector_code` (from the NACE and institutional-sector dictionaries of `get_brreg_dic()`). Other columns are never touched. Codes with no dictionary entry pass through unchanged, and labels are not codes, so applying `brreg_label()` twice is the same as applying it once. Attributes of the input (such as `total_matches` from `brreg_search()`) are preserved.

**Network access.** Legal-form and role dictionaries are bundled and never need the network. NACE and sector dictionaries come from the SSB KLASS API on first use in a session and are cached for the session; when KLASS cannot be reached, or `options(tidybrreg.offline = TRUE)` is set, the bundled English dictionaries are used instead and the result carries their vintage. See `get_brreg_dic()` for the full policy.

**Returns.** When `x` is a data frame: the same tibble with code columns replaced by labels. When `x` is a character vector: a character vector of labels, without names.

**Output shaping (server-side).** `.limit` rows (default 200), `.offset`, `.columns`, `.format` (records, csv, markdown). The structured result reports `n_total`, the attributes tidybrreg attached (for example `total_matches`, `complete`, `http_status`) and every warning tidybrreg signalled, with its condition class.

x.description: A tibble from `brreg_entity()`, `brreg_search()`, or `brreg_roles()`, or a character vector of codes.

dic.description: A character string naming the dictionary to use when `x` is a character vector. One of `"legal_form"`, `"nace"`, `"sector"`, `"role"`, `"role_group"`. Ignored when `x` is a data frame (dictionaries are inferred from column names).

code.description: For data frames: character vector of column names for which to retain the original code alongside the label. A column with suffix `_code` is added before the label column. For example, `brreg_label(x, code = "legal_form")` adds `legal_form_code`.

lang.description: Language for labels: `"en"` (default) or `"no"` (Norwegian, as published by BRREG and SSB).

.offset.description: Number of rows to skip before returning.

.columns.description: Columns to keep (tidybrreg's English column names). Default: all.

tools.name: brreg_prokura
tools.title: Retrieve procuration authority (prokura)
tools.description:
Fetch the registered procuration combinations for a Norwegian legal entity from the Brønnøysund Fullmakt service. Procuration is a commercial power of attorney under the Norwegian Powers of Attorney Act (prokuraloven): a holder may bind the entity in ordinary business, but not, absent separate authority, sell or encumber its real property. It is a narrower and separate mandate from the general signing authority returned by `brreg_signatur()`.

One row is returned per person within each registered combination.

**Person identification.** The Fullmakt service returns each person's name as a single string in `name`; it does not split it into given and family names, so no synthetic `person_id` is constructed. Join to `brreg_roles()` on `birth_date` together with `name` at query time if cross-referencing to the role network is required. Role designations are returned as English labels looked up from role_types, with the original Norwegian code preserved in `role_code`; the signing-mode designations (`SIGN`, `SIFE`, `SIHV`, `PROK`, `POFE`, `POHV`) are included in role_types alongside the board roles. Birth dates arrive as `DD.MM.YYYY` from this service and as ISO dates from the roles endpoint; both are parsed to `Date`, so the two join directly.

**Status handling.** The per-entity endpoints behind `brreg_roles()`, `brreg_roles_legal()`, `brreg_konsern()`, `brreg_signatur()` and `brreg_prokura()` share one contract. HTTP 404 means the organization number is unknown to that endpoint, which for konsern, signatur and prokura is the ordinary case of an entity with nothing registered there: the typed zero-row tibble is returned with attribute `http_status = 404L` and no warning. HTTP 410 means the entity has been deleted: the typed zero-row tibble is returned with `http_status = 410L`, `deletion_date`, and a `tidybrreg_warning_deleted`. Any other status of 400 or above aborts with a `tidybrreg_error_http`. A successful response with nothing registered returns the typed zero-row tibble with no attribute. Use `brreg_entity()` to distinguish a non-existent organization number from a live entity with nothing registered.

**Returns.** A tibble with the same columns as `brreg_signatur()`, with `signature_type` set to `"procuration"`. A zero-row tibble with the same typed columns if no procuration is registered.

**Output shaping (server-side).** `.limit` rows (default 200), `.offset`, `.columns`, `.format` (records, csv, markdown). The structured result reports `n_total`, the attributes tidybrreg attached (for example `total_matches`, `complete`, `http_status`) and every warning tidybrreg signalled, with its condition class.

tools.name: brreg_roles_legal
tools.title: Retrieve roles an entity holds in other entities
tools.description:
Reverse role lookup: find all entities where the given entity holds a role (e.g. parent company, shareholder, general partner). This is distinct from `brreg_roles()`, which returns who holds roles IN the given entity.

**Status handling.** The per-entity endpoints behind `brreg_roles()`, `brreg_roles_legal()`, `brreg_konsern()`, `brreg_signatur()` and `brreg_prokura()` share one contract. HTTP 410 means the entity has been deleted: the typed zero-row tibble is returned with `http_status = 410L`, `deletion_date`, and a `tidybrreg_warning_deleted`. Any other status of 400 or above aborts with a `tidybrreg_error_http`. A successful response with nothing registered returns the typed zero-row tibble with no attribute. Use `brreg_entity()` to distinguish a non-existent organization number from a live entity with nothing registered.

**Returns.** A tibble with one row per role held. Columns: `org_nr` (queried entity), `target_org_nr` (entity where role is held), `target_name`, `role_code`, `role`, `share` (ownership share if applicable), `deregistered`. tools.name: brreg_signatur
tools.title: Retrieve signature authority (signaturrett)
tools.description:
Fetch the registered signing combinations for a Norwegian legal entity from the Brønnøysund Fullmakt service. Signature authority determines who may bind the entity in general, and is distinct from the roles returned by `brreg_roles()`: an entity may have many board members yet a signing rule such as "the board jointly" or "the general manager alone".

Each registered combination (`combination_id`) carries a rule (`rule`, e.g. "Styret i fellesskap") and the persons who satisfy it. One row is returned per person within each combination.

**Person identification.** The Fullmakt service returns each person's name as a single string in `name`; it does not split it into given and family names, so no synthetic `person_id` is constructed. Join to `brreg_roles()` on `birth_date` together with `name` at query time if cross-referencing to the role network is required. Role designations are returned as English labels looked up from role_types, with the original Norwegian code preserved in `role_code`; the signing-mode designations (`SIGN`, `SIFE`, `SIHV`, `PROK`, `POFE`, `POHV`) are included in role_types alongside the board roles. Birth dates arrive as `DD.MM.YYYY` from this service and as ISO dates from the roles endpoint; both are parsed to `Date`, so the two join directly.

**Standardised vs registered rule.** `rule` and `combination_code` come from the registry's structured combination. Where the rule has been standardised (`rule_status` code `"RF"`) this is the registered rule. Where it has not (`"RI"`), the structured combination is the statutory default ("the board jointly") and the actually registered rule is the free text in `rule_text`; read `rule_text` in that case. `rule_text` may be `NA` when no free text is recorded.

**Status handling.** The per-entity endpoints behind `brreg_roles()`, `brreg_roles_legal()`, `brreg_konsern()`, `brreg_signatur()` and `brreg_prokura()` share one contract. HTTP 404 means the organization number is unknown to that endpoint, which for konsern, signatur and prokura is the ordinary case of an entity with nothing registered there: the typed zero-row tibble is returned with attribute `http_status = 404L` and no warning. HTTP 410 means the entity has been deleted: the typed zero-row tibble is returned with `http_status = 410L`, `deletion_date`, and a `tidybrreg_warning_deleted`. Any other status of 400 or above aborts with a `tidybrreg_error_http`. A successful response with nothing registered returns the typed zero-row tibble with no attribute. Use `brreg_entity()` to distinguish a non-existent organization number from a live entity with nothing registered.

**Returns.** A tibble with one row per person per signing combination. Columns: `org_nr`, `entity_name`, `signature_type` (`"signature"`), `rule_status`, `rule_text`, `combination_id`, `combination_code`, `rule`, `name`, `birth_date` (Date), `role_code`, `role`. A zero-row tibble with the same typed columns if the entity has no registered signing combination.

tools.name: brreg_update_fields
tools.title: Retrieve field-level CDC changes as a flat tibble
tools.description:
Returns one row per field-level change, plus one synthetic row for each event that carries no field patches (Ny, Sletting, Fjernet). Synthetic rows have `operation = NA`, `field = NA`, `path = NA`, `new_value = NA`, preserving event-level metadata in the output.

Patches are RFC 6902 operations. Nested values are flattened to one row per leaf; `path` keeps the raw JSON pointer of the leaf (for example `/forretningsadresse/adresse/0`) and `field` its snake_case rendering, so the register's own representation is never lost. A `move` emits an add at the destination and a `remove` at the source.

To retrieve initial field values for newly registered entities (change_type `"Ny"`), call `brreg_entity()` per org_nr — the CDC payload for Ny events contains no field-level patches.

**Time handling.** `since` is sent to the feed as a UTC instant. A `POSIXct` keeps its full precision; a `Date` is midnight UTC of that day; an ISO 8601 string (`"2026-03-01"` or `"2026-03-01T14:00:00Z"`) is parsed as UTC. Timestamps in the result are `POSIXct` in the `UTC` time zone, whatever the session time zone.

**Completeness.** The feed is read page by page until a page is short, the feed is exhausted, or `max_pages` is reached. The result carries attributes `complete` (`FALSE` when `max_pages` stopped the read while the last page was full, or a later page failed), `pages_fetched`, and `cursor` (the last `update_id` read; pass `update_id + 1` as the next cursor to resume). Stopping on `max_pages` signals a `tidybrreg_warning_truncated`; a failure after the first page signals a `tidybrreg_warning_partial` and returns the pages already read; a failure on the first page aborts with a `tidybrreg_error_http`.

**Unknown members.** Any member of an update object that the package does not model is passed through as a column named by its snake_case key, and the result carries attribute `unknown_members` plus a single `tidybrreg_warning_unknown_member`, so an upstream addition cannot vanish silently.

**Returns.** A tibble with columns: `update_id`, `org_nr`, `change_type`, `timestamp` (POSIXct, UTC), `operation`, `field`, `path`, `new_value`. No list-columns. Events without field patches appear as rows with `operation`, `field`, `path` and `new_value` all `NA`.

**Output shaping (server-side).** `.limit` rows (default 200), `.offset`, `.columns`, `.format` (records, csv, markdown). The structured result reports `n_total`, the attributes tidybrreg attached (for example `total_matches`, `complete`, `http_status`) and every warning tidybrreg signalled, with its condition class.

# brreg_download: Download the full Norwegian business register

Download a complete extract of the Central Coordinating Register for Legal Entities (~1 million entities, ~150 MB gzipped). The bulk endpoint does not support server-side filtering — it always returns all entities. Use `brreg_search()` for filtered queries up to 10,000 results, or download the full register here and filter locally.

## Backend routing

The brreg API has two data access paths with fundamentally different characteristics, following the cansim (Statistics Canada) pattern of separate functions for separate access patterns rather than the eurostat pattern of auto-routing within one function:

- **`brreg_search()`**: JSON API with server-side filtering. Fast for small result sets, capped at 10,000. Interactive exploration.
- **`brreg_download()`**: Bulk CSV or JSON. Always returns the full register. Appropriate for any analysis requiring more than 10,000 entities.

Results from both paths use the same column names and types via field_dict; only observed columns are emitted (see `brreg_entity()`).

## Caching

With `cache = TRUE` (default) the gzipped payload is stored in `tools::R_user_dir("tidybrreg", "cache")` together with a sidecar recording the server's `ETag` and `Last-Modified` validators, and a later call reuses it. `refresh = TRUE` forces a new download. `refresh = "auto"` sends a HEAD request and re-downloads when either validator differs from the sidecar; when the sidecar is missing or the server sends neither validator, nothing can prove the cache current, so it is re-downloaded. With `cache = FALSE` the payload goes to a temporary file that is deleted after parsing; with `type_output = "path"` that temporary path is returned and the caller owns it. The cache directory is created only by this function, never at load time.

Metadata of the most recent download (`url`, `etag`, `last_modified` as a UTC `POSIXct`, `downloaded_at`, `path`) is available as `attr(result, "brreg_download")` on tibble output.

## Arguments

- `type`: One of `"enheter"` (main entities, default), `"underenheter"` (sub-entities / establishments), or `"roller"` (all roles for all entities). Roller data is only available as JSON via `/roller/totalbestand` (~131 MB).
- `format`: Download format: `"csv"` (default for enheter/underenheter, comma-delimited) or `"json"` (JSON array). Only the JSON bulk carries `historiskeNavn`; the CSV has no such column. Roller bulk download is always JSON regardless of this parameter.
- `refresh`: `FALSE` (default): use cached file if available. `TRUE`: force re-download. `"auto"`: revalidate against the server and re-download only when the cached copy cannot be shown current. Any other value is an error.
- `cache`: Logical. If `TRUE` (default), keep the downloaded file in the persistent cache directory; if `FALSE`, use a temporary file.
- `type_output`: One of `"tibble"` (default) or `"path"` (returns the file path without parsing).

## Value

Depends on `type_output`:

- `"tibble"`: A tibble with ~1 million rows. Column names mapped via field_dict. For `type = "roller"`, one row per role assignment with the columns of `brreg_roles()`.
- `"path"`: Character file path to the gzipped download.

## See also

`brreg_search()` for filtered API queries, `brreg_updates()` for incremental changes since a given date.

Other tidybrreg entity functions: `brreg_children()`, `brreg_entity()`, `brreg_konsern()`, `brreg_prokura()`, `brreg_roles()`, `brreg_roles_legal()`, `brreg_search()`, `brreg_signatur()`, `brreg_underenheter()`, `brreg_update_fields()`, `brreg_updates()`

## Examples

```r
if (interactive() && curl::has_internet()) (if (getRversion() >= "3.4") withAutoprint else force)({ # examplesIf

# Download full register as tibble (~150MB download, ~1M rows) entities <- brreg_download()

# Just get the file path (no parsing) path <- brreg_download(type_output = "path")

# Force refresh entities <- brreg_download(refresh = TRUE)

}) # examplesIf
```

# brreg_entity: Look up a Norwegian legal entity

Retrieve registration details for a legal entity from Norway's Central Coordinating Register for Legal Entities (Enhetsregisteret), maintained by the Brønnøysund Register Centre. Every legal entity operating in Norway is assigned a unique 9-digit organization number and registered in this central register.

## Details

Column names are translated from Norwegian to English via the package field dictionary (field_dict). API fields not in the dictionary pass through with auto-generated snake_case names, so new fields added by brreg are never silently dropped. Use `brreg_label()` to translate coded values (legal forms, NACE codes) to English descriptions.

## Observed fields only

The register emits only the fields that apply to an entity: a sole proprietorship (`ENK`) typically carries no `founding_date` or `employees`, a foreign branch (`NUF`) no `municipality_code`. The returned columns are exactly the fields the response carried, so every column other than `org_nr`, `registry` and `deleted` is conditionally present. Test for a column with `"x" %in% names(result)` rather than assuming it.

## Deleted entities

BRREG reports a deleted entity either as HTTP 410 or, for most deletions, as HTTP 200 with `respons_klasse = "SlettetEnhet"` and a `slettedato`. Both are modelled the same way: `deleted` is `TRUE`, `deletion_date` is the parsed date, every other field the response carried is kept, and a `tidybrreg_warning_deleted` is signalled (silence it with `suppressWarnings(classes = "tidybrreg_warning_deleted")`). Live entities carry `deleted = FALSE`.

## Arguments

- `org_nr`: Character. A single 9-digit Norwegian organization number. Validated using `brreg_validate()` before the API call; a vector of several numbers is an error (iterate with `lapply()`).
- `registry`: One of `"auto"` (default, tries enheter then underenheter), `"enheter"` (main entities only), or `"underenheter"` (sub-entities only). Sub-entities have different fields (e.g. `overordnetEnhet` for the parent entity, `beliggenhetsadresse` instead of `forretningsadresse`).
- `type`: A type of variables: `"code"` (default) returns raw codes, `"label"` returns English labels for coded columns (legal form, NACE, sector, etc.), following the eurostat package's pattern. Labelling NACE and sector codes consults SSB KLASS on first use in a session; see `get_brreg_dic()`.

## Value

A tibble with one row and one column per field the API returned, named via field_dict, plus `registry` (which registry answered) and `deleted` (logical). Frequently present columns include `org_nr`, `name`, `legal_form`, `employees`, `founding_date`, `nace_1`, `municipality_code`, `bankrupt`, and `parent_org_nr`.

## See also

`brreg_search()` for querying multiple entities, `brreg_label()` for translating codes to English, field_dict for the column name mapping, tidybrreg_conditions for the errors and warnings signalled.

Other tidybrreg entity functions: `brreg_children()`, `brreg_download()`, `brreg_konsern()`, `brreg_prokura()`, `brreg_roles()`, `brreg_roles_legal()`, `brreg_search()`, `brreg_signatur()`, `brreg_underenheter()`, `brreg_update_fields()`, `brreg_updates()`

## Examples

```r
if (interactive() && curl::has_internet()) (if (getRversion() >= "3.4") withAutoprint else force)({ # examplesIf # Equinor ASA — Norway's largest company brreg_entity("923609016")

# With English labels (eurostat pattern) brreg_entity("923609016", type = "label")

# Or pipe to brreg_label() for more control brreg_entity("923609016") |> brreg_label(code = "legal_form") }) # examplesIf
```

# brreg_konsern: Retrieve the corporate group structure (konsernstruktur)

Fetch the registered group hierarchy for a Norwegian legal entity from the Enhetsregisteret konsernstruktur endpoint (added by BRREG 2026-06-24). The tree is returned flat: one row per node, root included at `level = 0`, each child carrying its link form (`knytningsform`, e.g. `KDAT` "Konsern datter"), ownership basis (`grunnlag`, e.g. `"100%"`), and the registration date of the relation.

## Details

The JSON response omits `knytningsform` on the root node while the API's CSV variant emits it as `KKKK` "Øverste mor"; the root row is synthesized here to match the CSV semantics.

This is the ownership hierarchy and is distinct from `brreg_children()`, which searches `overordnetEnhet` — the administrative parent relation used in public-sector (ORGL) structures, not konsern ownership.

## 404 semantics

The endpoint returns 404 both for organization numbers that do not exist and for live entities that are not part of any registered group — the common case for ordinary companies. The `in_corporate_group` column from `brreg_entity()` disambiguates the two without a second lookup here.

## Status handling

The per-entity endpoints behind `brreg_roles()`, `brreg_roles_legal()`, `brreg_konsern()`, `brreg_signatur()` and `brreg_prokura()` share one contract. HTTP 404 means the organization number is unknown to that endpoint, which for konsern, signatur and prokura is the ordinary case of an entity with nothing registered there: the typed zero-row tibble is returned with attribute `http_status = 404L` and no warning. HTTP 410 means the entity has been deleted: the typed zero-row tibble is returned with `http_status = 410L`, `deletion_date`, and a `tidybrreg_warning_deleted`. Any other status of 400 or above aborts with a `tidybrreg_error_http`. A successful response with nothing registered returns the typed zero-row tibble with no attribute. Use `brreg_entity()` to distinguish a non-existent organization number from a live entity with nothing registered.

## Arguments

- `org_nr`: Character. A single 9-digit organization number.

## Value

A tibble with one row per node in the group tree. Columns: `org_nr` (the queried entity), `node_org_nr`, `node_name`, `level` (0 for the root), `link_form`, `link_form_desc`, `basis`, `relation_date` (Date), `parent_org_nr`, `parent_name`, `legal_form`, `legal_form_desc`. A zero-row tibble with the same typed columns if no group structure is registered.

## See also

`brreg_children()` for the ORGL administrative hierarchy, `brreg_entity()` for the `in_corporate_group` flag, `brreg_roles_legal()` for roles an entity holds in others.

Other tidybrreg entity functions: `brreg_children()`, `brreg_download()`, `brreg_entity()`, `brreg_prokura()`, `brreg_roles()`, `brreg_roles_legal()`, `brreg_search()`, `brreg_signatur()`, `brreg_underenheter()`, `brreg_update_fields()`, `brreg_updates()`

## Examples

```r
if (interactive() && curl::has_internet()) (if (getRversion() >= "3.4") withAutoprint else force)({ # examplesIf brreg_konsern("923609016") # Equinor ASA }) # examplesIf
```
docs.brreg_label:
# brreg_label: Translate codes to human-readable labels

Replace coded values in a brreg tibble with English (or Norwegian) descriptions, following the eurostat package's `label_eurostat()` pattern. Works on both data frames and character vectors.

## Which columns are labelled

`legal_form` (from legal_forms), `role_code` (from role_types), `role_group_code` (from role_groups), `nace_1`, `nace_2`, `nace_3` and `sector_code` (from the NACE and institutional-sector dictionaries of `get_brreg_dic()`). Other columns are never touched. Codes with no dictionary entry pass through unchanged, and labels are not codes, so applying `brreg_label()` twice is the same as applying it once. Attributes of the input (such as `total_matches` from `brreg_search()`) are preserved.

## Network access

Legal-form and role dictionaries are bundled and never need the network. NACE and sector dictionaries come from the SSB KLASS API on first use in a session and are cached for the session; when KLASS cannot be reached, or `options(tidybrreg.offline = TRUE)` is set, the bundled English dictionaries are used instead and the result carries their vintage. See `get_brreg_dic()` for the full policy.

## Arguments

- `x`: A tibble from `brreg_entity()`, `brreg_search()`, or `brreg_roles()`, or a character vector of codes.
- `dic`: A character string naming the dictionary to use when `x` is a character vector. One of `"legal_form"`, `"nace"`, `"sector"`, `"role"`, `"role_group"`. Ignored when `x` is a data frame (dictionaries are inferred from column names).
- `code`: For data frames: character vector of column names for which to retain the original code alongside the label. A column with suffix `_code` is added before the label column. For example, `brreg_label(x, code = "legal_form")` adds `legal_form_code`.
- `lang`: Language for labels: `"en"` (default) or `"no"` (Norwegian, as published by BRREG and SSB).

## Value

When `x` is a data frame: the same tibble with code columns replaced by labels. When `x` is a character vector: a character vector of labels, without names.

## See also

legal_forms, role_types, role_groups for bundled reference data, `get_brreg_dic()` for fetching fresh dictionaries.

Other tidybrreg utilities: `brreg_validate()`, `get_brreg_dic()`, `tidybrreg_conditions`, `tidybrreg_endpoints`

## Examples

```r
if (interactive() && curl::has_internet()) (if (getRversion() >= "3.4") withAutoprint else force)({ # examplesIf eq <- brreg_entity("923609016")

# Label all code columns brreg_label(eq)

# Keep original codes alongside labels brreg_label(eq, code = "legal_form")

# Label a character vector directly brreg_label(c("AS", "ASA", "ENK"), dic = "legal_form") brreg_label(c("AS", "ASA", "ENK"), dic = "legal_form", lang = "no") }) # examplesIf
```

# brreg_prokura: Retrieve procuration authority (prokura)

Fetch the registered procuration combinations for a Norwegian legal entity from the Brønnøysund Fullmakt service. Procuration is a commercial power of attorney under the Norwegian Powers of Attorney Act (prokuraloven): a holder may bind the entity in ordinary business, but not, absent separate authority, sell or encumber its real property. It is a narrower and separate mandate from the general signing authority returned by `brreg_signatur()`.

## Details

One row is returned per person within each registered combination.

## Person identification

The Fullmakt service returns each person's name as a single string in `name`; it does not split it into given and family names, so no synthetic `person_id` is constructed. Join to `brreg_roles()` on `birth_date` together with `name` at query time if cross-referencing to the role network is required. Role designations are returned as English labels looked up from role_types, with the original Norwegian code preserved in `role_code`; the signing-mode designations (`SIGN`, `SIFE`, `SIHV`, `PROK`, `POFE`, `POHV`) are included in role_types alongside the board roles. Birth dates arrive as `DD.MM.YYYY` from this service and as ISO dates from the roles endpoint; both are parsed to `Date`, so the two join directly.

## Status handling

The per-entity endpoints behind `brreg_roles()`, `brreg_roles_legal()`, `brreg_konsern()`, `brreg_signatur()` and `brreg_prokura()` share one contract. HTTP 404 means the organization number is unknown to that endpoint, which for konsern, signatur and prokura is the ordinary case of an entity with nothing registered there: the typed zero-row tibble is returned with attribute `http_status = 404L` and no warning. HTTP 410 means the entity has been deleted: the typed zero-row tibble is returned with `http_status = 410L`, `deletion_date`, and a `tidybrreg_warning_deleted`. Any other status of 400 or above aborts with a `tidybrreg_error_http`. A successful response with nothing registered returns the typed zero-row tibble with no attribute. Use `brreg_entity()` to distinguish a non-existent organization number from a live entity with nothing registered.

## Arguments

- `org_nr`: Character. A single 9-digit organization number.

## Value

A tibble with the same columns as `brreg_signatur()`, with `signature_type` set to `"procuration"`. A zero-row tibble with the same typed columns if no procuration is registered.

## See also

`brreg_signatur()` for general signing authority.

# brreg_roles: Retrieve board members, officers, and auditors

Fetch all registered roles for a Norwegian legal entity. Returns one row per role assignment. Person-held roles include name and birth date. Entity-held roles (auditor firms, accountants) include the entity's organization number.

## Details

Role types and groups are returned as English labels looked up from the package's role_types and role_groups reference datasets. Original Norwegian codes are preserved in `role_code` and `role_group_code`.

## Person identification

The `person_id` column is a synthetic key composed of birth date, last name, first name, and middle name. It enables network analysis across companies but has a non-trivial collision risk for common Norwegian names sharing a birth date. The brreg public API does not expose national identity numbers.

## Status handling

# brreg_search: Search Norwegian legal entities

Query the Central Coordinating Register by name, legal form, industry, geography, and other criteria. Results are paginated automatically up to `max_results`.

## Norwegian legal forms

Common codes for the `legal_form` parameter:

- **AS**: Private limited company (like UK Ltd, German GmbH)
- **ASA**: Public limited company (like UK PLC, German AG)
- **ENK**: Sole proprietorship
- **NUF**: Norwegian-registered foreign entity (branch office)

See legal_forms for the complete list with English translations.

## Result window

The search endpoints allow a page size of up to 10,000 but reject any page where `size * (page + 1)` exceeds 10,000 (observed 2026-08-08: a Bergen municipality query reported 57,954 matches; result 10,001 answered HTTP 400 `size * (page+1) kan ikke overstige 10_000`). A query matching more entities than that window cannot be retrieved completely through search. When the register reports more matches than the window and `max_results` asks for more than the window, the call aborts with a `tidybrreg_error_result_window` before any page is returned; narrow the query (for example by `municipality_code`, `legal_form` or `nace_code`), or use `brreg_download()` for the full register. When `max_results` is at or below the window the first `max_results` matches are returned and the result carries `complete = FALSE` plus a `tidybrreg_warning_truncated` whenever more matches exist.

## Arguments

- `name`: Character. Entity name (partial match, case-insensitive).
- `legal_form`: Character. Legal form code: `"AS"`, `"ASA"`, `"ENK"`, etc. See legal_forms for valid codes.
- `municipality_code`: Character. 4-digit Norwegian municipality code.
- `nace_code`: Character. NACE industry code (e.g. `"64.190"`).
- `min_employees`: Integer. Employee count range.
- `max_employees`: Integer. Employee count range.
- `bankrupt`: Logical. If `TRUE`, return only bankrupt entities. Only supported for `registry = "enheter"`; supplying it for `"underenheter"` is an error.
- `parent_org_nr`: Character. Filter to subsidiaries of this org.
- `max_results`: Integer. Maximum entities to return (default 200). Values above the 10,000 result window are allowed but abort when the register reports more matches than the window can deliver.
- `registry`: One of `"enheter"` (main entities, default) or `"underenheter"` (sub-entities / establishments). Sub-entities use `beliggenhetsadresse.kommunenummer` instead of `kommunenummer` for geographic filtering, and the `bankrupt` parameter is not available.
- `type`: A type of variables: `"code"` (default) returns raw codes, `"label"` returns English labels for coded columns.

## Value

A tibble with one row per entity. Column names follow the package field dictionary (field_dict); only observed fields are emitted (see `brreg_entity()`). Attributes: `total_matches`, the number of matches the register reported, and `complete`, `FALSE` when fewer rows were returned than matched. A valid empty result is a zero-row tibble with character columns `org_nr`, `name` and `legal_form`.

## See also

`brreg_entity()` for single lookups, `brreg_label()` for translating codes to English, tidybrreg_conditions for the errors and warnings signalled.

Other tidybrreg entity functions: `brreg_children()`, `brreg_download()`, `brreg_entity()`, `brreg_konsern()`, `brreg_prokura()`, `brreg_roles()`, `brreg_roles_legal()`, `brreg_signatur()`, `brreg_underenheter()`, `brreg_update_fields()`, `brreg_updates()`

```r
# Large private companies in Oslo brreg_search(legal_form = "AS", municipality_code = "0301", min_employees = 500, max_results = 10) }) # examplesIf
```

# brreg_signatur: Retrieve signature authority (signaturrett)

Fetch the registered signing combinations for a Norwegian legal entity from the Brønnøysund Fullmakt service. Signature authority determines who may bind the entity in general, and is distinct from the roles returned by `brreg_roles()`: an entity may have many board members yet a signing rule such as "the board jointly" or "the general manager alone".

## Details

Each registered combination (`combination_id`) carries a rule (`rule`, e.g. "Styret i fellesskap") and the persons who satisfy it. One row is returned per person within each combination.

## Person identification

The Fullmakt service returns each person's name as a single string in `name`; it does not split it into given and family names, so no synthetic `person_id` is constructed. Join to `brreg_roles()` on `birth_date` together with `name` at query time if cross-referencing to the role network is required. Role designations are returned as English labels looked up from role_types, with the original Norwegian code preserved in `role_code`; the signing-mode designations (`SIGN`, `SIFE`, `SIHV`, `PROK`, `POFE`, `POHV`) are included in role_types alongside the board roles. Birth dates arrive as `DD.MM.YYYY` from this service and as ISO dates from the roles endpoint; both are parsed to `Date`, so the two join directly.

## Standardised vs registered rule

`rule` and `combination_code` come from the registry's structured combination. Where the rule has been standardised (`rule_status` code `"RF"`) this is the registered rule. Where it has not (`"RI"`), the structured combination is the statutory default ("the board jointly") and the actually registered rule is the free text in `rule_text`; read `rule_text` in that case. `rule_text` may be `NA` when no free text is recorded.

## Status handling

The per-entity endpoints behind `brreg_roles()`, `brreg_roles_legal()`, `brreg_konsern()`, `brreg_signatur()` and `brreg_prokura()` share one contract. HTTP 404 means the organization number is unknown to that endpoint, which for konsern, signatur and prokura is the ordinary case of an entity with nothing registered there: the typed zero-row tibble is returned with attribute `http_status = 404L` and no warning. HTTP 410 means the entity has been deleted: the typed zero-row tibble is returned with `http_status = 410L`, `deletion_date`, and a `tidybrreg_warning_deleted`. Any other status of 400 or above aborts with a `tidybrreg_error_http`. A successful response with nothing registered returns the typed zero-row tibble with no attribute. Use `brreg_entity()` to distinguish a non-existent organization number from a live entity with nothing registered.

## Arguments

- `org_nr`: Character. A single 9-digit organization number.

## Value

A tibble with one row per person per signing combination. Columns: `org_nr`, `entity_name`, `signature_type` (`"signature"`), `rule_status`, `rule_text`, `combination_id`, `combination_code`, `rule`, `name`, `birth_date` (Date), `role_code`, `role`. A zero-row tibble with the same typed columns if the entity has no registered signing combination.

docs.brreg_update_fields:
# brreg_update_fields: Retrieve field-level CDC changes as a flat tibble

Returns one row per field-level change, plus one synthetic row for each event that carries no field patches (Ny, Sletting, Fjernet). Synthetic rows have `operation = NA`, `field = NA`, `path = NA`, `new_value = NA`, preserving event-level metadata in the output.

## Details

Patches are RFC 6902 operations. Nested values are flattened to one row per leaf; `path` keeps the raw JSON pointer of the leaf (for example `/forretningsadresse/adresse/0`) and `field` its snake_case rendering, so the register's own representation is never lost. A `move` emits an add at the destination and a `remove` at the source.

To retrieve initial field values for newly registered entities (change_type `"Ny"`), call `brreg_entity()` per org_nr — the CDC payload for Ny events contains no field-level patches.

## Time handling

`since` is sent to the feed as a UTC instant. A `POSIXct` keeps its full precision; a `Date` is midnight UTC of that day; an ISO 8601 string (`"2026-03-01"` or `"2026-03-01T14:00:00Z"`) is parsed as UTC. Timestamps in the result are `POSIXct` in the `UTC` time zone, whatever the session time zone.

## Completeness

The feed is read page by page until a page is short, the feed is exhausted, or `max_pages` is reached. The result carries attributes `complete` (`FALSE` when `max_pages` stopped the read while the last page was full, or a later page failed), `pages_fetched`, and `cursor` (the last `update_id` read; pass `update_id + 1` as the next cursor to resume). Stopping on `max_pages` signals a `tidybrreg_warning_truncated`; a failure after the first page signals a `tidybrreg_warning_partial` and returns the pages already read; a failure on the first page aborts with a `tidybrreg_error_http`.

## Unknown members

Any member of an update object that the package does not model is passed through as a column named by its snake_case key, and the result carries attribute `unknown_members` plus a single `tidybrreg_warning_unknown_member`, so an upstream addition cannot vanish silently.

## Arguments

- `since`: Date, POSIXct, or ISO 8601 string. Return updates at or after this instant. Defaults to yesterday (midnight UTC).
- `size`: Integer. Number of updates per page (max 10000).
- `max_pages`: Integer. Maximum pages to fetch. Default 1. Set higher to paginate through large result sets automatically.
- `type`: One of `"enheter"` or `"underenheter"`.
- `verbose`: Logical. Print page-level progress.

## Value

A tibble with columns: `update_id`, `org_nr`, `change_type`, `timestamp` (POSIXct, UTC), `operation`, `field`, `path`, `new_value`. No list-columns. Events without field patches appear as rows with `operation`, `field`, `path` and `new_value` all `NA`.

## See also

`brreg_updates()` for the event-level view.

Other tidybrreg entity functions: `brreg_children()`, `brreg_download()`, `brreg_entity()`, `brreg_konsern()`, `brreg_prokura()`, `brreg_roles()`, `brreg_roles_legal()`, `brreg_search()`, `brreg_signatur()`, `brreg_underenheter()`, `brreg_updates()`

# collapse_observed: Collapse an observed array value to a single character cell

BRREG returns addresses, `vedtektsfestetFormaal`, and `aktivitet` as arrays of register line-fragments. Element text routinely contains commas and semicolons but never newlines, so `"\n"` is the only separator that survives a round trip: a consumer can split it back into the observed elements, which `"; "` and `", "` do not allow. Arrays whose elements are objects (`historiskeNavn`, `paategninger`) have no meaningful text join and are serialized to JSON instead, preserving field structure.

Note that the CSV bulk is BRREG's own flattening and uses field-specific separators (newline for addresses, space for wrapped text such as `vedtektsfestetFormaal`), so CSV-sourced and JSON-sourced values for those fields are not byte-identical and cannot be made so without imposing a per-field rule.

# get_brreg_dic: Fetch a brreg dictionary

Retrieve English or Norwegian label dictionaries for NACE industry codes (SSB classification 6, SN2007) or institutional sector codes (SSB classification 39). Dictionaries are cached in a session-level environment (following the eurostat package pattern), so the network is consulted at most once per dictionary and language per session.

## Network access and offline use

With `source = "auto"` (default) the dictionary is requested from the SSB KLASS API (`data.ssb.no`), which is the only source of Norwegian labels and of codes valid today. If the request fails, the bundled English dictionary is returned instead and a `tidybrreg_warning_bundled_fallback` states its vintage; for `lang = "no"` there is no bundled fallback and the error propagates. `source = "bundled"` never touches the network and is the mode to use offline or in tests; `options(tidybrreg.offline = TRUE)` makes it the default for the session. `source = "klass"` requires the network and errors when it is unavailable. The bundled dictionaries were retrieved from KLASS on 2026-06-16 (see tidybrreg_provenance).

## Arguments

- `dictname`: One of `"nace"` or `"sector"`.
- `lang`: `"en"` (default) for English labels or `"no"` for Norwegian.
- `source`: One of `"auto"`, `"klass"`, or `"bundled"`; see the section on network access.
- `refresh`: Logical. If `TRUE`, ignore the session cache and fetch again.

## Value

A tibble with columns `code`, `name` (label in the requested language), and `level`. Attributes `source` (`"klass"` or `"bundled"`), `lang`, and `vintage` (the date the labels were retrieved from KLASS) record where the labels came from.

## See also

`brreg_label()` for translating columns in place, tidybrreg_provenance for the bundled dictionaries' sources.

Other tidybrreg utilities: `brreg_label()`, `brreg_validate()`, `tidybrreg_conditions`, `tidybrreg_endpoints`

## Examples

```r
get_brreg_dic("nace", source = "bundled") attr(get_brreg_dic("sector", source = "bundled"), "vintage") if (interactive() && curl::has_internet()) (if (getRversion() >= "3.4") withAutoprint else force)({ # examplesIf get_brreg_dic("nace", lang = "no") }) # examplesIf
```

docs.tidybrreg_conditions:
# tidybrreg_conditions: Conditions signalled by tidybrreg

Every error and warning raised by the package carries a class that can be caught with `tryCatch()` or silenced with `suppressWarnings()` selectively, and a set of fields describing the request that produced it. All classes inherit from `tidybrreg_error` or `tidybrreg_warning`.

## Errors

- `tidybrreg_error_invalid_org_nr`: the organization number failed `brreg_validate()`. Field `org_nr`.
- `tidybrreg_error_invalid_filter`: a filter is not supported by the requested registry (for example `bankrupt` on `underenheter`). Fields `registry`, `filter`.
- `tidybrreg_error_not_found`: the endpoint answered HTTP 404 for an organization number. Fields `org_nr`, `endpoint`, `status`.
- `tidybrreg_error_http`: any other HTTP status of 400 or above, or a failure on the first page of a paginated request. Fields `endpoint`, `status`, `messages` (as extracted from the BRREG error body).
- `tidybrreg_error_result_window`: the query matches more entities than BRREG's search window can deliver and the request asked for more than the window. Fields `endpoint`, `total_matches`, `retrieval_limit`, `filters`. See `brreg_search()`.

## Warnings

- `tidybrreg_warning_deleted`: the entity has been deleted from the register (HTTP 410, or HTTP 200 with `respons_klasse` `"SlettetEnhet"`). Fields `org_nr`, `deletion_date`.
- `tidybrreg_warning_partial`: a paginated request failed after at least one page was retrieved; the partial result is returned with attribute `complete = FALSE`. Fields `endpoint`, `status`, `pages_fetched`.
- `tidybrreg_warning_truncated`: more results exist than were returned because of `max_results` or `max_pages`; the result carries attribute `complete = FALSE`. Fields `endpoint`, `returned`, `total_matches`.
- `tidybrreg_warning_unknown_member`: an update feed carried a member the package does not model; it is passed through unchanged. Field `members`.
- `tidybrreg_warning_bundled_fallback`: SSB KLASS was unreachable and a bundled dictionary was used instead. Fields `dictname`, `vintage`.
- `tidybrreg_warning_parse`: values could not be coerced to the type declared in field_dict; the result carries attribute `brreg_parse_problems`. Field `n`.

## See also

Other tidybrreg utilities: `brreg_label()`, `brreg_validate()`, `get_brreg_dic()`, `tidybrreg_endpoints`

## Examples

```r
tryCatch( brreg_entity("123456789"), tidybrreg_error_invalid_org_nr = function(e) e$org_nr )
```
docs.tidybrreg_endpoints:
# tidybrreg_endpoints: Retrieval limits of the register endpoints

One row per endpoint reachable through the fifteen exports, with the pagination model, the retrieval window, and how the package behaves at the boundary. The evidence column separates what BRREG documents (<https://data.brreg.no/enhetsregisteret/api/dokumentasjon/>) from what has been observed against the live service; limits observed for one route are never assumed for another. Boundary probes for the search routes run in the scheduled live test workflow (`tests/testthat/test-liveapi-audit.R`).

## Enhetsregisteret API

Base URL `https://data.brreg.no/enhetsregisteret/api`.

| Route | Function | Pagination | Limits and boundary | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `GET /enheter/{orgnr}` | `brreg_entity()` | none | 200 (entity or `SlettetEnhet`), 404 unknown, 410 deleted | documented; 200-with-`SlettetEnhet` observed on 25/25 recent deletions (2026-08) |
| `GET /underenheter/{orgnr}` | `brreg_entity()` | none | as enheter | documented |
| `GET /enheter?...` | `brreg_search()`, `brreg_children()` | `page`/`size`; `page.totalElements` reported | `size` at most 10,000; `size * (page + 1)` at most 10,000, else HTTP 400; the package aborts with `tidybrreg_error_result_window` when `total_matches` exceeds the window and more was requested | observed 2026-08-08 (Bergen query: 57,954 matches; result 10,000 retrievable, 10,001 answered 400) |
| `GET /underenheter?...` | `brreg_search()`, `brreg_underenheter()` | as enheter | as enheter; no `konkurs` filter (the package rejects `bankrupt`) | documented; window probed in the live suite |
| `GET /enheter/{orgnr}/roller` | `brreg_roles()` | none (whole payload) | 404 unknown entity, 410 deleted; empty `rollegrupper` for an entity without roles | documented |
| `GET /roller/enheter/{orgnr}/juridiskeroller` | `brreg_roles_legal()` | none | 404 when nothing is registered | documented |
| `GET /konsernstruktur/{orgnr}` | `brreg_konsern()` | none (recursive tree) | 404 both for unknown numbers and for entities in no group; depth observed to 6 | documented; depth observed (ASA census, 2026-10) |
| `GET /oppdateringer/enheter`, `/oppdateringer/underenheter` | `brreg_updates()`, `brreg_update_fields()` | cursor: `dato` for the first page, `oppdateringsid` (exclusive) thereafter; `size` at most 10,000 | no documented window; field patches (`includeChanges`) available from 2025-09 | documented; cursor semantics observed |
| `GET /oppdateringer/roller` | `brreg_updates()` with `type = "roller"` | `afterTime` for the first page, `afterId` thereafter; `size` at most 10,000 | CloudEvents without field detail | documented; `afterId` pagination not yet probed live |
| `GET /enheter/lastned/csv`, `/enheter/lastned`, `/underenheter/lastned/csv`, `/underenheter/lastned`, `/roller/totalbestand` | `brreg_download()` | none (one gzipped file) | regenerated nightly; `ETag` and `Last-Modified` sent | documented; sizes observed 2026-08 (152 / 196 / 59 / 75 / 131 MB) |
| `GET /organisasjonsformer` | build script only | none | 44 codes | observed 2026-06-16 |

## Fullmakt service

Base URL `https://data.brreg.no/fullmakt`.

| Route | Function | Pagination | Limits and boundary | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `GET /enheter/{orgnr}/signatur` | `brreg_signatur()` | none | 404 when nothing is registered (common for ENK) | documented |
| `GET /enheter/{orgnr}/prokura` | `brreg_prokura()` | none | 404 when nothing is registered | documented |

## SSB KLASS (not BRREG)

Base URL `https://data.ssb.no/api/klass/v1`.

| Route | Function | Pagination | Limits and boundary | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `GET /classifications/6/codesAt`, `/classifications/39/codesAt` | `get_brreg_dic()` | none | whole code list for a date and language | observed 2026-06-16 |

## Rate limiting

BRREG publishes no rate limit or rate-limit headers; the package throttles itself to 5 requests per second per host and retries 429 and 503 up to three times. Request timeouts are httr2's defaults.

## See also

Other tidybrreg utilities: `brreg_label()`, `brreg_validate()`, `get_brreg_dic()`, `tidybrreg_conditions`

# tidybrreg_provenance: Provenance of the bundled reference data

Every table shipped with tidybrreg is listed here with its source, licence, vintage, the transformations applied, and how the package uses it. The tables are regenerated by `data-raw/build_dictionaries.R`; the vintages below are the dates of the last regeneration that touched each table, taken from the repository history.

## Exported datasets (data/)

- **field_dict**: **Package-authored.** A mapping from BRREG JSON paths and CSV column headers to English column names and R types, written by the package author from the Enhetsregisteret API documentation (<https://data.brreg.no/enhetsregisteret/api/dokumentasjon/>) and from fields observed on live responses. The Norwegian paths are BRREG's identifiers; the English names and types are the author's editorial choices and carry the package's MIT licence. Last revised 2026-06-16. Used at runtime by every parser.
- **legal_forms**: **BRREG code list plus manual translation.** `code`, `name_no` and `expired` are retrieved from `GET https://data.brreg.no/enhetsregisteret/api/organisasjonsformer`, published by the Brønnøysund Register Centre under the Norwegian Licence for Open Government Data (NLOD) 2.0 (<https://data.norge.no/nlod/en/2.0>); `name_en` is a manual translation by the package author (unreviewed by BRREG), falling back to `name_no` for codes without a translation. Retrieved 2026-06-16. Used by `brreg_label()`.
- **role_types**: **Package-authored from BRREG documentation.** Codes and Norwegian descriptions follow the role codes listed in the Enhetsregisteret roller documentation and the Fullmakt service; English names are a manual translation by the package author. BRREG publishes no machine-readable role code list with translations. Last revised 2026-06-16. Used by `brreg_roles()`, `brreg_roles_legal()`, `brreg_signatur()`, `brreg_prokura()` and `brreg_label()`.
- **role_groups**: **Package-authored from BRREG documentation.** As role_types, for role group (`rollegruppe`) codes. Last revised 2026-06-16. Used by `brreg_roles()` and `brreg_label()`.

## Internal fallback dictionaries (R/sysdata.rda)

- **`nace_codes`**: **Statistics Norway (SSB) KLASS classification 6** (Standard Industrial Classification SN2007), English labels, retrieved from `https://data.ssb.no/api/klass/v1/classifications/6/codesAt` on 2026-06-16 (the effective date of the codes is that retrieval date). SSB publishes KLASS classifications as open data under NLOD 2.0 according to its data licence page (<https://www.ssb.no/en/omssb/tjenester-og-verktoy/api/klass-api>); the maintainer has not obtained a separate confirmation, so the statement is reproduced as published. Used only when SSB KLASS is unreachable or `source = "bundled"` is requested in `get_brreg_dic()`; the returned tibble carries `vintage`.
- **`sector_codes`**: **SSB KLASS classification 39** (institutional sector), English labels, same source, licence statement, retrieval date and use as `nace_codes`.

## Register data

Entity, role, group, signature and update data retrieved at runtime come from the Brønnøysund Register Centre's open APIs and are licensed under NLOD 2.0; the licence requires attribution to the Brønnøysund Register Centre when the data are redistributed. KLASS labels retrieved at runtime are Statistics Norway's.

## See also

Other tidybrreg reference data: `field_dict`, `legal_forms`, `role_groups`, `role_types`
